topic: Using std::istream::unget() to Push Back Characters into Input Stream
explanation: In C++, the 'unget()' member function of 'std::istream' allows the programmer to push back a single character onto the input stream, effectively 'unreading' it. This is useful in parsing scenarios where a character read ahead needs to be reconsidered or reprocessed. Modern C++ handles stream states and exceptions carefully, and 'unget()' interacts with the stream buffer to restore characters, potentially throwing exceptions if stream state changes occur. Proper use of 'unget()' ensures flexible and robust input handling in C++ programs.
